data.title: Global Silicon Wafer Supply Gap Seen Widening Through 2028
data.description:
The global silicon wafer supply gap is expected to widen as HBM and sub-2-nanometer advanced logic capacity expands, with the shortfall projected to grow from about 8% at the end of 2026 to 15% in 2027 and 24% in 2028. According to ChainCatcher, analysts said GlobalWafers, Wafer Works, and Sino-American Silicon Products could benefit, while the second half of 2027 through the first half of 2028 may see another round of shortages if supply growth fails to keep pace.

SEMI said global silicon wafer shipments reached 3.573 billion square inches in the second quarter of 2026, up 9.1% quarter over quarter and 7.4% year over year. Analysts estimated global 12-inch silicon wafer monthly capacity at about 10.69 million wafers in 2026, rising 7% year over year, then increasing only about 3% to 11 million wafers in 2027 and about 6% to 11.7 million to 11.76 million wafers in 2028.

The expected new supply includes about 300,000 wafers from the initial phase of GlobalWafers' second stage and about 100,000 wafers from Wafer Works. Analysts also projected HBM silicon wafer consumption to rise 23% in 2027 and 28% in 2028, while new DRAM capacity is expected to add about 350,000 to 450,000 wafers per month by 2028. Logic process wafer consumption is forecast to grow 12% in 2027 and 11% in 2028. Customer wafer inventories remain at about 100 to 120 days, above the normal 50 to 70 days.

data.title: GEOPOLITICS | Singapore Air Quality Deteriorates to Worst Level Since 2019
data.description:
Singapore is shrouded in haze as smoke from wildfires in neighboring Indonesia pushed islandwide pollution to levels that pose a health risk, according to Bloomberg.

Gabrielle Ng has more.

data.title: Bank of England Reportedly Considers Halting Sales of Long-Dated Gilts
data.description:
As long-dated U.K. government bond yields have climbed to multi-decade highs, the Bank of England may soon stop selling the long-dated gilts it bought during the financial crisis and the COVID-19 pandemic. According to Sina Finance, officials from the Bank of England, the U.K. Treasury, and the U.K. Debt Management Office have drafted related plans, but the source of the report was not disclosed.

Market participants expect the Bank of England to slow the pace of balance-sheet reduction to 50 billion pounds a year over the 12 months starting in October, which would leave active bond sales at about 20 billion pounds. Long-dated gilts account for about 20% of the Bank of England's current active bond sales, so even if sales stop, the impact on the overall pace of quantitative tightening would be limited.

The Bank of England's Monetary Policy Committee is due to decide on next year's quantitative tightening plan on Thursday. The central bank is facing larger losses because prices of 20-year and 30-year U.K. government bonds have fallen sharply, and the 30-year gilt yield is currently around 5.9%, near its highest level since the 1990s.

data.title: GEOPOLITICS | Japan Cabinet Approves Temporary Food Sales Tax Cut to 1%
data.description:
Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi’s cabinet approved a plan to temporarily cut Japan’s consumption tax on food to 1%, according to Bloomberg.

The move brings the government closer to fulfilling a key election pledge to ease household pressure from the soaring cost of living.

data.title: DeepSeek Engineer Says AI May Match His Kernel Optimization Skills Within a Year
data.description:
DeepSeek engineer Liu Sheng said AI is advancing fast enough that it could match or surpass his ability to write kernels within six months to a year. According to ChainCatcher, he wrote that DeepSeek V4.1's main Attention kernel was written by him, but AI has already progressed from helping him search documentation and debug code to reading CUDA, PTX, and SASS, analyzing instruction stalls, and independently optimizing kernels.

Liu said he expects AI to next design scheduling plans, evaluate performance, and complete implementations on its own. He added that improving kernels at DeepSeek speeds up both training and inference, which in turn helps AI catch up faster, but said he will keep optimizing as long as other companies' models continue advancing.

He said he is unlikely to lose his job, but may be forced to shift from writing kernels by hand to operating agents. Liu also said his main concern is not losing his livelihood, but possibly never again having the chance to do work he enjoys. He said he remains at DeepSeek because he believes frontier AI should be open and affordable for everyone, and said he does not believe Anthropic or OpenAI can achieve that. He warned that if the most powerful AI is controlled by only a few companies, the technology gap could widen into a gap in power and social class.

data.title: BofA Sees Brent Oil Could Reach $150 on Infrastructure Risk
data.description:
Bank of America Securities commodities and derivatives research head Francisco Blanch said Brent oil prices could rise to as much as $150 a barrel if critical infrastructure, including Saudi Arabia's East-West pipeline, is hit on a more permanent basis, according to Bloomberg.

Blanch made the comments on Bloomberg Television.

data.title: AI TRENDS | GSK Agrees to Buy Experimental Blood Cancer Drug for Up to $750 Million
data.description: According to Wallstreetcn, GSK agreed to buy an experimental blood cancer drug from the unlisted Chinese biotech company Enmu Biotech for up to $750 million and plans to test it for multiple myeloma, with early clinical trials set to begin next year.

data.title: Zama Opens Deposits Into 16 Confidential Morpho Vaults on Ethereum
data.description: Zama is opening deposits into 16 confidential Morpho vaults on Ethereum on Sept. 15. According to NS3.AI, the company is also launching a protocol for confidential swaps between assets and vault shares on Ethereum. Zama said its first vault reached $40 million in total value locked within seven weeks.

data.title: UK Energy Bills Seen Rising 25% in January as Inflation Pressures Build
data.description:
UK household energy bills are forecast to rise about 25% in January as the war in Iran pushes up wholesale gas and electricity prices, according to Bloomberg Economics.

The increase is expected to add to inflationary pressures across the wider economy.

data.title: STOCKS | Fourier Shares Surge 28.6% On Heavy Turnover
data.description:
Fourier (03625) jumped as much as 33% to an intraday high of HK$81.95, before easing to HK$79, up 28.6%, according to ETNet.

The stock traded as low as HK$60 and crossed above its 10-day moving average of HK$74.625. Turnover reached 1.151 million shares worth HK$79.17 million, with an active buy-sell ratio of 52:48 and net active buying of HK$3.3447 million. China Investment Information was the largest net passive buyer at HK$2.1752 million, while JPMorgan was the largest net passive seller at HK$4.4691 million.

data.title: S&P Flags Credit, Earnings Risks at Indonesia’s State Banks
data.description: Indonesia’s state-owned banks face rising credit and earnings risks after government-driven lending pushed loan growth to more than twice the industry pace, according to Bloomberg reported S&P Global Ratings.

data.title: AI | Biren Technology Weighs $1 Billion Share Sale
data.description: Shanghai Biren Technology Co. is considering another share sale to help fund its artificial intelligence ambitions, according to Bloomberg. People familiar with the matter said the Chinese AI chip company is weighing a transaction that could raise about $1 billion.

data.title: OIL | Saudi East-West Pipeline May Stay Partly Offline for Three to Five Weeks
data.description:
Saudi Arabia's East-West pipeline was severely damaged after a drone attack, and most of its capacity is expected to take three to five weeks to recover. According to Sina Finance, repairs may allow partial operations during that period, but it is still unclear how much crude can be transported, and the Saudi government and Saudi Aramco have not confirmed a specific restart time.

Two regional officials familiar with the repair assessment said the damage involved a major pumping station, while some damaged equipment may take longer to restore. The attack took place on September 10 and involved several pipeline facilities in the Riyadh and Medina regions, causing injuries. Saudi Arabia said the drones were launched from Iraq, and at the request of Iraq's prime minister, it has not taken retaliatory action for now.

Rystad Energy estimated that the pipeline has been carrying about 2.6 million to 4 million barrels of crude per day since late August. The pipeline links Saudi Arabia's eastern oil fields with the Red Sea port of Yanbu and has a maximum design capacity of 7 million barrels per day. Brent crude rose more than 2% on Monday and traded near $109 a barrel as supply concerns increased.

data.title: STOCKS | Nikkei Ends Flat After V-Shape Rebound as Defense Spending Outlook Hits Bonds
data.description:
Japan's Nikkei average ended little changed at 63,484.10 on September 15, 2026, after opening down 0.5% at 63,190.37. According to Sina Finance, the index was dragged lower early by electronics and metals before recovering losses later in the session.

Japan's bond market fell sharply as expectations for higher defense spending rattled markets. According to Sina Finance, people familiar with the matter said Japan is considering setting its medium-term defense spending target at 3.5% of GDP to keep pace strategically with NATO and other U.S. allies.

Japan's Finance Minister Satsuki Katayama said the government will review and cut redundant subsidies and tax breaks, and she rejected issuing new debt to fund a consumption tax cut. According to Sina Finance, she also said current tax revenue is expected to come in slightly above forecasts.

Japan's 30-year government bond yield rose 5.5 basis points to 4.12%, while the 10-year yield climbed 4 basis points to 3.025%.

data.title: Oxford Economics Says China Thaw Could Lift Indian Manufacturing
data.description:
The thaw in India-China relations could give New Delhi room to ease restrictions on Chinese investment and draw a larger share of global capital, according to Oxford Economics.

Oxford Economics said the shift may support Indian manufacturing, Bloomberg reported.

data.title: Monad Co-Founder Highlights Rising Aggregator Spoofing in Uniswap v4 Hooks
data.description:
Monad co-founder Keone Hon said 0x published an article this morning about a new pattern that first appeared in PropAMM and has now spread to Uniswap v4 Hooks. According to Odaily, the article says malicious market makers alternate between extremely tight and extremely wide quotes to lure aggregators, then widen spreads after trades are routed, while some Hooks switch fees between 0% and 18%.

Hon said Solana published a similar article months ago about comparable behavior on Solana aggregators, though the fee cap was around 1%, and later removed it. He added that open systems are meant to eliminate intermediaries and hidden fees, but aggregator spoofing creates a large hidden tax that can only be addressed through fully on-chain order routing.

0x also said malicious Uniswap v4 Hooks have increased recently. It said some Hooks offer attractive prices during quoting, then change execution prices at settlement to take funds from users through aggregators, wallets, and trading apps.

data.title: STOCKS | Metlen Chief Warns Europe Could Lose Key High-Tech Metals Race
data.description:
A FTSE 100 energy group warned that Europe may still lose the competition for metals needed by high-tech industries, even if the region can produce enough critical metals to meet its own demand. According to Sina Finance, Metlen Chairman Evangelos Mytilineos said European companies are unwilling to pay higher prices for gallium, which the company plans to start producing next year, and prefer cheaper supply.

Mytilineos warned that if Europe cannot build stable, systematic domestic demand, the metal will be sold outside Europe to buyers in the United States and Japan. He also said Metlen plans to produce 50 tons of gallium a year, with about one-quarter already sold to an unnamed U.S. technology company, while two other potential non-European deals are under discussion.

Fastmarkets' Henry Sanderson said the United States is pouring in huge sums to catch up with market leaders, while Europe has not taken similar action. ProjectBlue founder Jack Bedder said Japan has invested in critical materials supply chains for years, while recent U.S. intervention in the market is one of the biggest commodity-market moves in a generation.

data.title: USDC On-Chain Transaction Volume Tops $100 Trillion
data.description: USDC’s cumulative on-chain transaction volume has surpassed $100 trillion as of September 12, 2026, according to a post by USDC’s official account on X. According to ChainCatcher, the stablecoin has long been used to support money transfers at internet scale.

data.title: STOCKS | China Life Falls 3% As Hang Seng Index Drops 0.9%
data.description:
China Life Insurance (02628) fell as much as 3.02% to HK$28.86, breaking below its 20-day moving average of HK$29.289, according to ETNet.

The stock last traded at HK$28.90, down 3.02%, after 23.95 million shares changed hands for HK$703 million. The active buy-sell ratio was 42:58, with net active selling of HK$101 million. Hang Seng Index was down 0.9% at 24,703, while the Hang Seng China Enterprises Index fell 0.9% to 8,207.

data.title: STOCKS | Westpac Says Japan's Extra Defense Spending Will Worsen U.S. Treasury Yield Pain
data.description: Westpac Banking Corporation said Japan's possible extra defense spending will deepen pain in the bond market and affect global bonds. According to Sina Finance, Martin Whetton, head of financial markets strategy at the bank, said Federal Reserve rate hikes and persistently higher oil prices will push U.S. Treasury yields higher again, and that the move toward 5% during Monday's trading session should be seen as normal rather than exceptional. The 10-year U.S. Treasury yield rose nearly 3 basis points to 5.01%.
